doc.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021

title: Closing remarks and Zoom
summary: The two thank each other, discuss Zoom's value for education and interviews, and say goodbye.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well it’s been a great gig for me, and I appreciate your time today, and there’s a lot more we can touch on and maybe we’ll do so again. And I thank you for your time.
Oh my pleasure, are you kidding? Thank you for doing this. It’s an honor.
Well great. I hope we can cross paths. You know I usually do these things face to face but obviously we deal with the times we’re in.

Yeah. Well you know I mean Zoom has been a lifesaver in so many ways. I mean it’s basically enabled us to keep our education system going during this past year or so whereas otherwise things would have come to a screeching halt. So I mean that’s been important. And you know also I mean it enables, you’ve done a number of these interviews lately on Zoom that you wouldn’t have had a chance to do face to face. So I mean that was a good move on your part just to switch to that medium.
Well I’m going to pause our recording and I hope whatever arrangement is bouncing around in your head after we’re doing reaches a fine conclusion.
Thank you. If you get to New York, for whatever reason, please let me know and let’s hook up. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
Thank you. Take good care. © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-
